manc.name: Mancunian
manc.about: Manchester's own English: flat vowels, "our kid" for a brother or a mate, and everything good is mint, sound or dead nice.

no: Don't worry about it, don't bother

greet: Oh hello, how are you doing?
Alright, love? Haven't seen you in ages.
reply: Can't complain. Well, I could, but I won't.
sunny: Sun's out in Manchester. Mark it on the calendar.
Lovely day. Everyone's out in Piccadilly Gardens.
Make the most of it, it won't last.
rain: It's that fine rain that soaks you right through.
Never trust a dry morning round here.
bye: Right, I'll let you go. Ta-ra!
busy: Sorry, can't stop, the tram's due.
Running late, the trains out of Piccadilly are a mess.
Got a meeting in Spinningfields, talk later?
Can't stop, I'm parked on a meter.
Sorry, flat out today. Message me.

greet: Ey, look who it is! You alright?
Alright, kid? Long time no see.
sunny: Mint weather, this. Get out in it.
rain: I'm wet through, kid. Got drenched coming down the ginnel.
busy: Sorry, I'm up to my eyes today.
I'm dead busy, catch you later.

touts: The next stop is Piccadilly Gardens.
Please take all your belongings with you when leaving the tram.
A busker on Market Street: "Any requests? Not Wonderwall, I've done it three times already."
Three for a pound, three for a pound!
hawkers: Buy the Big Issue street magazine
Get your scarves, get your hats!
Football scarves and hats on match day
Three punnets of fruit for two pounds
small_talk: Tram's packed again, there must be a match on.
Have you been to the new place in Ancoats? Queue round the corner.
Everyone says it always rains here. To be fair, it does.
The Curry Mile was heaving last night.
Afflecks still has the best weird stuff in town.
Half the people I know work at MediaCity now.
Traffic on the Mancunian Way was a joke this morning.
The yellow buses are proper handy now.
Shall we get a brew before the meeting?
Northern Quarter on a Saturday is something else.
